title: Hubble Space Telescope
note: Hubble as it is now, after Servicing Mission 4 (May 2009): SA3 rigid arrays, Soft Capture Mechanism on the aft bulkhead, NOBL covers on the bay doors. Body stations and appendage positions from Lockheed's 1985 handbook drawings (structure unchanged since launch). Frame in facts.frame: z = V1 (aft bulkhead at 0), x = V2, y = V3.

solar_array_panels.value: 4 panels per wing; GaAs cells on a Kapton face sheet over aluminium honeycomb; anti-sun side white Tedlar; graphite mast with gold-anodised handles through an MLI blanket

sources.quote: four panels were mounted onto each
The anti-sun sides of the panels are white Tedlar to serve as radiators to space.
The Mast is a M55J graphite-composite cylinder with two gold-anodized handles protruding through a MLI blanket.

magnetic_torquers.layout_source: lmsc1985, drawing 4171929 sh.2 (forward end view, 6.19 px/in on the 3400 px scan): four bars lying across the body, centres 65 in out at about 33, 147, 231, 303 deg, spanning about 50 in; lmsc1985, drawing 4171929 sh.1 (side view, 6.02 px/in on the 3400 px scan): slanted, about 58 in along V1, aft end toward the nearer V3 side. Bar diameter about 3 in (scaled). lmsc1985 p.3-5 says '90 deg apart'; the drawing's bars are not evenly spaced, the drawing wins here

sources.quote: SCUFF PLATE(4) TWO SHOWN-STA 535 TWO AT STA 240
scuff plates, large protective metal plates on struts that extend approximately 30 in. from the surface

scuff_plates.layout_source: sm4_photos s125e011763 (from +V3): gold strut frames at both edges, so on +-V2; s125e012031: round gold plates about 0.6 m across (138 px/m against the aft bulkhead)

equipment_bays.value: 10 equipment bays plus 2 trunnion bays; bay doors flat honeycomb except curved covers on Bays 6 and 9 (reaction wheels)
equipment_bays.quote: This section contains 10 bays for equipment and two bays to support aft trunnion pins and scuff plates.

sources.quote: the crew uses 225 ft of handrails encircling the spacecraft. For visibility, the rails are painted yellow.
There was a dramatic peeling of the paint on one handrail

thermal_blankets.value: MLI on light shield and forward shell, outer layer 127 um aluminised Teflon FEP over 15 embossed aluminised Kapton layers; silvered FOSR tape on aft shroud and aft bulkhead; aluminium FOSR on the door's sun side, door inside and light shield inside flat black

sources.quote: The insulation blankets are 15 layers of aluminized Kapton, with an outer layer of aluminized Teflon flexible optical solar reflector (FOSR). Aluminized or silvered flexible reflector tape covers most of the remaining exterior.
Silvered FOSR tape on the aft shroud and aft bulkhead exteriors
the 17-layer MLI blanket's outer layer (space-exposed) is 127 µm (0.005") Teflon FEP
many areas of the aluminized Teflon outer blanket layer had significant cracks

nobl.value: stainless-steel foil covers on picture frames over equipment bay doors; SM4 added Bays 8 and 5 (pre-flight plan)

sources.quote: The covers are made of specially coated stainless steel foil which is trimmed to fit each particular equipment bay door
The NOBL material selected was 0.1mm stainless steel coated with vapor deposited silver
The concave primary mirror—94.5 inches (2.4 meters) in diameter
The truss, 16 ft (4.8 m) long and 9 ft (2.7 m) in diameter

foil_look.value: The light shield and forward shell blankets are visibly wrinkled and crinkled silver; the aft shroud is flatter, bluish silver tape panels; yellow handrails; NASA 'worm' logo on the light shield.

nasa_model_b.value: 819k triangles in 57k loose pieces, no materials, 6.35 m overall in its file; aft skin missing

logo.source: sm4_photos, s125e011763 (from +V3): light shield edges at columns 1260 and 1788 (171 px/m on its 1.544 m radius), columns unrolled onto the cylinder; worm letters span columns 1359 to 1652 (1.82 m of arc), ESA mark 1657 to 1706; logo centre row 782 against the near front edge at row 575 (not corrected for the camera's tilt: estimate). Decal canvas covers columns 1345 to 1715, rows 720 to 845
logo.artwork: NASA worm and old ESA logo from Wikimedia Commons (NASA_Worm_logo.svg, ESA_logo.svg, in refs/hubble/logo); the worm keeps its own proportions, sized to the photo's width; the ESA ring and its 'esa' are placed separately, ring above text, as on the telescope

lga_forward.source: lmsc1985, drawing 4171929 sh.2 (forward end view, 6.19 px/in on the 3400 px scan): horn at 318 deg, 66 in out; lmsc1985, drawing 4171929 sh.1 (side view, 6.02 px/in on the 3400 px scan): at the light shield's front, pointing forward (station estimated); same size as the aft LGA (assumed)

grapple_fixtures.source: lmsc1985, drawing 4171929 sh.2 (forward end view, 6.19 px/in on the 3400 px scan): at 46.00 +Y (V2), its base 62 in toward -V3, base about 19 in wide and pin about 15 in (scaled). A second fixture by 180 deg symmetry: sm3aguide says two, next to the HGA drives, and s125e011763 shows the arm grappled on the +V3 side toward -V2
grapple_fixtures.quote2: The outer skin has two grapple fixtures next to the HGA drives

aperture_door_shape.source: sm4_photos s125e012031: the open door is round on its free end and square on the hinge side, with 16 tape strips running across the hinge, a white beam along the hinge edge, two gold handholds near the side edges and a white block on the free edge; lmsc1985 doc p.3-3 names the 'Hinge-Line Beam'; drawing 4171929 sh.1 puts the 'APERTURE DOOR LATCH(1)' opposite the hinge. Beam, latch and handhold sizes and places estimated from the photo

open_questions: SA3: where the wing's 7.1 m starts (mast vs panels), mast length, and whether SA3 uses the original pivot at STA 320. Fit from photos.
Handrail cross-section and standoff height: not found; measure from photos against known sizes.
NOBL sizes and which bays carry one after SM4 (sources disagree on 3A/3B bays; SM4 plan: Bays 8 and 5).
Colours (MLI silver, aft shroud FOSR, yellow handrails, solar cells, NOBLs): to sample from the SM4 photos.
Low-gain antennas, magnetometers, sun sensors, grapple fixture, trunnions: positions from the drawing, sizes from photos.
Wrinkled foil: no document describes wrinkles (they say 'cracked', 'curled'); the look comes from the SM4 photos.
HGA boom length: the drawing labels the dish at 232.30 in from the axis, but scaling the drawing by the door gives about 185 in, and s125e012031 (unfitted) suggests about 4.5 m; kept the label.
Sun sensors (2 fwd, 2 aft): drawing 4171929 sh.2 points at about 171 deg but gives no stations; not modelled.
